01-041.title: Measure natural ice before stepping onto it; avoid river ice and fishing holes
01-041.costSummary: A supervised rink costs little extra. Natural ice requires measuring equipment, rescue picks, and repeated checks.
01-041.benefitSummary: Official guidance sets minimum thickness thresholds, but ice can vary sharply across a small area. White ice is weaker than clear new ice, and river currents and fishing holes add hazards.
01-041.applicability: Thickness thresholds are not guarantees of safety. The original source includes cold-water rescue guidance and directs bystanders to the emergency chapter.

01-042.title: Use an angle grinder only with its guard and face protection; never fit a toothed wood blade
01-042.costSummary: Eye and face protection costs a modest amount; checks and safe setup add a minute or two each use.
01-042.benefitSummary: High-speed discs can shatter or kick back. Safety agencies recommend the correct guard and disc, eye and face protection, a stable two-handed grip, and using a saw for wood.
01-042.applicability: The evidence is safety guidance and incident reports, not a measured estimate of injuries prevented. The original source retains the equipment limits and incident references.

01-043.title: Ask someone in distress directly whether they have thought about suicide
01-043.costSummary: No money; it takes a question, time to listen, and the courage to begin a difficult conversation.
01-043.benefitSummary: Research has not found that asking about suicide creates more suicidal thoughts or distress. Some studies found less distress among students already at elevated risk.
01-043.applicability: The cited studies mainly tested questionnaires and research interviews, not conversations between friends. If someone says they may be in immediate danger, stay with them and connect them to crisis or emergency help.

02-043.title: Discuss bothersome menopause symptoms with a clinician; do not self-medicate or use hormones to prevent heart disease
02-043.costSummary: A clinical visit and follow-up are required; treatment suitability depends on medical history and personal risks.
02-043.benefitSummary: Hormone therapy reduced hot-flash frequency in trials, while some serious risks increased. Long-term trial data did not show an overall mortality benefit, and therapy is not recommended to prevent chronic disease.
02-043.applicability: The trial population and regimens differ from many people seeking symptom relief today. A clinician should assess individual benefits, contraindications, and alternatives.

02-044.title: Count dog walks as exercise if you already want a dog; do not get one just to live longer
02-044.costSummary: Dog ownership brings ongoing food, veterinary, licensing, care, and daily time costs for the animal's lifetime.
02-044.benefitSummary: Some observational studies associate dog ownership with lower mortality, but better-adjusted studies find little or no difference. The evidence does not show that getting a dog causes longer life.
02-044.applicability: The source treats the association as disputed and notes substantial confounding. Consider a dog for reasons that account for its welfare and long-term care, not as a longevity treatment.

03-025.title: Treat period pain and seek gynecological care when symptoms disrupt life or do not improve
03-025.costSummary: Pain medicine costs a small amount; assessment may require an appointment, imaging, and time.
03-025.benefitSummary: Trials found anti-inflammatory pain medicines can reduce menstrual pain. Persistent pain, deep pain during sex, or symptoms that disrupt school or work warrant medical assessment for causes such as endometriosis.
03-025.applicability: Medication can have side effects and is unsuitable for some people. Ask a clinician or pharmacist about personal risks, pregnancy, and other medicines.

05-045.title: Do not treat cryptocurrency as a protected investment in Mainland China
05-045.costSummary: Avoiding a purchase costs no money, though it also means not participating in a price rise.
05-045.benefitSummary: Mainland Chinese notices state that virtual currencies are not legal tender and prohibit related financial activities. Some civil transactions may be treated as invalid, leaving losses with the parties.
05-045.applicability: This is a jurisdiction-specific legal summary, not a prediction about every dispute. The original entry cites the relevant notices and court case; check current local rules before acting.

05-046.title: For self-employed pension contributions, compare the minimum tier and payback period before enrolling
05-046.costSummary: Contributions require substantial recurring payments and may be inaccessible until retirement eligibility.
05-046.benefitSummary: The source's model finds that the minimum contribution tier reaches its estimated break-even point after roughly ten years of benefits; paying more can take longer to recoup.
05-046.applicability: This estimate depends on Mainland China policy, contribution history, local wages, retirement age, and future rules. It is not a personalized pension projection.

06-029.title: Do not rely on lifting-posture training alone to prevent back pain; reduce heavy, repeated lifting and exercise
06-029.costSummary: Reducing load and repetition may require work changes; regular exercise takes ongoing time.
06-029.benefitSummary: The reviewed evidence did not show that lifting-technique training alone prevents back pain. Heavier and more frequent lifting was associated with greater risk, while regular exercise was associated with fewer episodes.
06-029.applicability: These findings do not establish an individual diagnosis or replace workplace safety controls. The original source distinguishes associations from causal evidence.

06-030.title: Do not expect calcium or bone broth to make a fracture heal faster
06-030.costSummary: No extra supplement cost is needed unless a clinician identifies a specific need.
06-030.benefitSummary: Trials have not shown that vitamin D improves fracture healing, and evidence on combined calcium and vitamin D is limited. People with a deficiency or osteoporosis may need different care.
06-030.applicability: Follow the treating clinician's fracture and nutrition advice. The source does not argue against treating a documented deficiency.

08-045.title: Do not lend your face, identity, or verification code for someone else's loan
08-045.costSummary: Declining costs nothing; verifying a request may take a few minutes and an uncomfortable conversation.
08-045.benefitSummary: If a loan is taken in your name, you may be the borrower rather than a witness or guarantor. A private promise from the acquaintance may not protect you from the lender.
08-045.applicability: This is a Mainland China legal and financial risk summary. Read the original court sources and seek qualified help before signing or sharing credentials.

08-046.title: Use working door and window locks and lock them; a single alarm may not deter burglary
08-046.costSummary: Locks and a motion light cost some money; locking up takes seconds.
08-046.benefitSummary: The cited UK studies associate door and window locks, especially with exterior lighting, with lower burglary risk. An alarm alone did not show the same association in the cited comparison.
08-046.applicability: The studies concern burglary, not robbery when residents are present, and do not guarantee prevention.

09-024.title: Do not repost or translate copyrighted comics, films, or books without permission
09-024.costSummary: Getting permission or choosing original material takes time; avoiding unauthorized distribution costs nothing.
09-024.benefitSummary: Sharing an unauthorized translation or copy can infringe copyright even when it is free. Advertising, subscriptions, or large-scale distribution can add criminal exposure under Mainland Chinese law.
09-024.applicability: Legal thresholds and penalties depend on facts and current law. The original entry cites statutes and cases; obtain legal advice for a real dispute.

09-025.title: Get permission before commercializing a fan work, or create genuinely original characters and relationships
09-025.costSummary: Seeking permission or redesigning a work takes time; litigation can be far more costly.
09-025.benefitSummary: A commercial work may infringe copyright by reusing protected characters and relationships, even when the wording is new. A cited Chinese case ended with substantial damages after years of litigation.
09-025.applicability: Free fan works are fact-specific, and the source says courts assess them individually. This summary is not legal advice.

09-026.title: Do not carry weapons such as batons, stun devices, knives, or pepper spray for self-defense
09-026.costSummary: Not buying or carrying one costs nothing; checking local rules takes little time.
09-026.benefitSummary: The source reports that carrying certain controlled items can lead to detention, with stricter penalties in transit hubs. Bringing a weapon into a conflict can also cause severe criminal consequences.
09-026.applicability: This is a Mainland China legal summary; item classifications and circumstances matter. Do not use it to assess another jurisdiction.

11-018.title: Do not build or distribute tools that skip or block another app's advertisements
11-018.costSummary: Avoiding the project costs no money; legal review and compliance work require time.
11-018.benefitSummary: Chinese courts have treated some ad-skipping or ad-blocking tools as unfair competition, including cases involving unpaid tools and monetary damages.
11-018.applicability: Outcomes depend on how a tool works and the parties involved. The original entry cites the decisions and applicable statute.

11-019.title: Do not resell overseas AI model access through an unlicensed proxy service
11-019.costSummary: Not launching avoids infrastructure, compliance, and customer-data handling costs.
11-019.benefitSummary: The source describes a Shanghai operator detained for 37 days in connection with an AI proxy service and reports national security warnings about unlicensed services and user data.
11-019.applicability: Detention is not a conviction. The source distinguishes the reported case from official risk guidance; current licensing rules require local legal review.

12-024.title: Before paying a store operator or dropshipping trainer, ask about later fees and where sales come from
12-024.costSummary: Checking the business model costs little; outsourced operations and training can demand repeated payments.
12-024.benefitSummary: Some schemes collect a small initial fee, then demand upgrade packages, inventory advances, or release fees while displaying fabricated orders. Paid fake-order boosting can itself be unlawful.
12-024.applicability: The source warns about documented scam patterns rather than claiming every store service is fraudulent. Verify the operator, contract, revenue source, and refund terms.

14-010.title: Do not send code, secrets, or private data to an unknown AI proxy
14-010.costSummary: Using an authorized provider and redacting sensitive material may take extra setup time.
14-010.benefitSummary: A proxy can view or alter prompts and responses. The cited study tested more than 400 services and found some that inserted malicious code or tampered with planted cloud credentials.
14-010.applicability: Treat the study as a sample, not a rate for every proxy. Use trusted providers, protect credentials, and review commands before granting software permission to run them.

17-010.title: For older adults walking a dog, hold the leash in the palm, keep it short, and train against lunging
17-010.costSummary: Changing grip and shortening the leash are free; training takes time and may require paid help.
17-010.benefitSummary: US emergency data show dog-walking falls and leash-related hand injuries among older adults. The source recommends a palm grip, a shorter leash, and training to reduce sudden pulling.
17-010.applicability: The cited studies count injuries but do not measure how many the proposed practices prevent. Choose a dog and walking setup the person can safely manage.

19-019.title: When changing cities for work, transfer pension and medical-insurance records instead of withdrawing early
19-019.costSummary: The transfer is free but requires an application and processing time after enrolling in the new location.
19-019.benefitSummary: Mainland Chinese social-insurance rules allow pension and employee medical-insurance histories to transfer and contribution periods to accumulate. A coverage gap can create a reimbursement waiting period.
19-019.applicability: Rules vary by age, province, enrollment type, and current policy. Confirm the process and any gap consequences with the local social-insurance office.

20-014.title: During vegan pregnancy or breastfeeding, discuss reliable vitamin B12 and infant feeding with a clinician
20-014.costSummary: A daily B12 supplement costs a modest amount; planning suitable infant foods requires attention.
20-014.benefitSummary: Vitamin B12 is scarce in unfortified plant foods. Untreated deficiency can harm infant growth and neurological development; the source recommends reliable B12 and appropriate complementary foods.
20-014.applicability: Well-planned vegan diets can be possible with reliable supplementation and professional guidance. Do not infer a diagnosis or change a child's diet from this summary alone.

24-012.title: Before dental implants, check what the bundled price includes and verify the clinic's pricing commitment
24-012.costSummary: Checking the public clinic list and asking for an itemized quote takes a few minutes and no fee.
24-012.benefitSummary: After China's centralized procurement, the cited source reports lower average prices for routine implants. The advertised bundle may exclude extraction, bone grafting, or other procedures.
24-012.applicability: Price caps and insurance coverage depend on provider type, location, and procedure. Ask for a written itemized plan and discuss suitable alternatives with a dentist.

27-017.title: During pregnancy, you do not need to rehome a cat; delegate litter cleaning and prevent infection through food and soil hygiene
27-017.costSummary: Delegating litter cleaning costs nothing; disposable gloves are inexpensive if no one else can do it.
27-017.benefitSummary: The cited studies did not find that owning a cat itself raises toxoplasmosis risk. Undercooked meat and contaminated soil were more relevant exposures; pregnancy can make first infection serious.
27-017.applicability: Follow prenatal-care guidance. The source recommends daily litter changes, handwashing, thoroughly cooked meat, and asking a clinician about testing or individual concerns.

28-009.title: Use an orthodontist for an in-person exam and follow-up; do not self-treat with mail-order aligners
28-009.costSummary: Professional care costs more and requires follow-up visits over the treatment period.
28-009.benefitSummary: Chinese device guidance calls for an orthodontist's supervision and regular review. The US FDA says it has not authorized clear aligners sold directly without a prescription and dental supervision.
28-009.applicability: This entry cites regulatory guidance, not an estimated complication rate. Ask a qualified dental professional about diagnosis and treatment options.

30-018.title: Do not send a child to a closed boot camp to stop internet use through harmful confinement or punishment
30-018.costSummary: Avoiding an unverified program costs nothing and avoids tuition; finding appropriate support takes time.
30-018.benefitSummary: Mainland China's Minors Protection Law prohibits methods that harm a child's physical or mental health. The source documents court cases involving serious abuse and criminal convictions at training schools.
30-018.applicability: The source recommends bringing an already-confined child home and seeking appropriate medical or child-protection help if abuse is reported. This is not a substitute for local legal or clinical support.
